Unit 5 • HL

Scalable Data Systems

Introduction

How do we handle Data at Global Scale?

This unit prepares you for the world of Big Data. You will move far beyond simple tables to explore Distributed Systems, NoSQL architectures, and the complex trade-offs between Consistency (ACID) and Availability (CAP Theorem).

You'll start by mastering critical reliability with Transactions (ACID). Then you'll break the single-server limit with Distributed Databases, before exploring modern alternatives like NoSQL and Data Mining.

Transactions (ACID)

Banking relies on this. A group of operations (Transfer: -100 here, +100 there) must succeed or fail as a UNIT.

  • Atomicity: All or nothing.
  • Consistency: The DB remains valid.
  • Isolation: Transactions don't interfere.
  • Durability: Once saved, it's saved forever.

Distributed Databases

When one server isn't enough. We split the data across the world.

  • Replication: Copying data to multiple locations (Safety).
  • Fragmentation: Splitting a table into pieces (Speed).
  • Trade-off: Keeping copies in sync is HARD (CAP Theorem).

NoSQL & Modern Models

SQL is rigid. Sometimes we need flexibility.

  • Document Stores (JSON): Flexible structure (e.g., MongoDB).
  • Key-Value: Ultra-fast lookups (e.g., Redis).
  • Graph: Storing relationships (e.g., Social Networks).

Data Intelligence (Mining)

Turning raw data into knowledge.

  • Data Warehouse: A massive archive of historical data.
  • ETL: Extract, Transform, Load (Cleaning the data).
  • Data Mining: Using algorithms to find hidden patterns (e.g., "People who buy diapers also buy beer").

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
TransactionA sequence of database operations treated as a single logical unit.
ACIDThe set of properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) that guarantee database reliability.
Data WarehouseA large, centralized repository of data integrated from disparate sources, used for analysis.
Data MiningThe process of discovering patterns, correlations, and anomalies within large datasets.
Distributed DatabaseA database in which storage devices are not all attached to a common processor (geographic spread).
ReplicationThe process of sharing information to ensure consistency between redundant resources.
NoSQLNon-relational databases designed for unrelated, unstructured, or rapidly changing data.
OLAPOnline Analytical Processing. Technology used to organize large business databases and support complex analysis.

Common Misconceptions

NoSQL is always faster

It can be faster for simple reads/writes, but it often lacks the strict safety guarantees (ACID) of SQL.

Data Mining = Searching

Searching finds a known record. Mining finds UNKNOWN patterns (e.g., predicting customer churn).

Distributed means Instant

Speed of light is real. Updating a copy in Tokyo takes time to reach New York (Eventual Consistency).

Syllabus Coverage

  • A3.3.4 Transactions & ACID
  • A3.4.1 Distributed & NoSQL
  • A3.4.2 Data Warehousing
  • A3.4.3 Data Mining

Real-World Uses

  • Global Banking (ACID)
  • Social Media Feeds (Graph DB)
  • E-commerce Recommendations (Mining)
  • Real-time Gaming (Key-Value Stores)
  • Business Intelligence Dashboards (OLAP)

Think Deeper

"The Cost of Truth" In a distributed world, it's faster to verify a lie than to wait for the truth. Does 'Eventual Consistency' mean we can never truly trust the state of the Global Network?
